title: BO112-SARC-004_baseline-1
characteristics_ch1: sorted population: live cell tumor digest
extract_protocol_ch1: Tumor samples were minced and up to 1 gram of tumor was placed in a GentleMACS C tube with RPMI, Collagenase D (1mg/mL), and DNase I (0.3mg/mL) and dissociated using a GentleMACS Octo Dissociator for 1hr at 37C. Cells were washed and filtered through a 100-micron strainer to obtain a single cell suspension. Cells were treated with RBC lysis buffer (BD) for 5 mins at room temperature. Live cells were isolated using a magnetic column based live cell isolation kit. For one tumor (RT-001), CD45+ and CD45- cells were further isolated using an antibody based magnetic isolation.

Single cell gene expression libraries were created using Chromium Next GEM Single Cell 3' (v3.1 Chemistry) (10x Genomics), Chromium Next GEM Chip G Single Cell Kit (10x Genomics), and Single Index Kit T Set A (10x Genomics) according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Briefly, cells were loaded to target 10,000 cells to form GEMs and barcode individual cells. GEMs were then cleaned cDNA and libraries were also created according to manufacturer’s instructions. Library quality was assessed using 4200 TapeStation System and D1000 ScreenTape (both from Agilent) and Qubit 2.0 (Invitrogen) for concentration and size distribution. Samples were sequenced using NextSeq500 (Illumina) with 75 PE reads.  Samples were demultiplexed with Cell Ranger mkfastq (10x Genomics).
data_processing: The demultiplexing, barcoded processing, gene counting and aggregation were made using the 10x genomics cellranger-7.0.1.
Assembly: GRCh38
Supplementary files format and content: barcodes.tsv.gz, features.tsv.gz, matrix.mtx.gz files

title: BO112-SARC-004_baseline_T1
extract_protocol_ch1: Tissues were formalin fixed and paraffin embedded.
Spatial transcriptomic profiling was performed using the 10x Genomics Visium HD platform on four FFPE longitudinal tumor specimens from a single patient.
data_processing: Regions of interest were selected based on H&E quality and IHC data on immune cell infiltration from adjacent sections. RNA quality was confirmed by DV200 assessment prior to processing.

Two specimens were placed per Visium HD slide (6.5 × 6.5 mm capture area), and libraries were prepared according to the manufacturer’s protocol (Visium HD CytAssist Spatial GEX 6.5 mm workflow; 10x Genomics).
Libraries underwent Qubit fluorometric quantification and TapeStation fragment analysis and were sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq (PE50), generating ~550M reads per sample.
FASTQ files were processed using Space Ranger (v4.0.1) with alignment to the GRCh38-2020-A reference and quantification using the Visium Human Transcriptome Probe Set v2.0.

CytAssist alignment images were registered to corresponding brightfield H&E images using the supplied JSON files with manual refinement using loupe Browser 9. Resulting feature matrices and spatial metadata were used for downstream analysis.
All four specimens were imported into Seurat, and one baseline sample with low transcript capture was excluded. Cells expressing <50 unique genes were removed.
Remaining cells were normalized using SCTransform with cell area (total 2-µm bins per cell) regressed as a technical covariate.
Cell clustering (resolution 0.8) and differential expression analysis enabled manual cell-type annotation.
Tumor cell identity was confirmed via inferCNV using immune cells as reference.
Putative T–myeloid doublets were subclustered (resolution 0.3) and reannotated. Final annotated cell maps were exported for spatial visualization in Loupe Browser.
Assembly: GRCh38

title: BO112-SARC-004_surgery_T4
characteristics_ch1: treatment: Radiation (6 Gy x 5), BO-112 (3 doses)
extract_protocol_ch1: Tissues were formalin fixed and paraffin embedded.
Spatial transcriptomic profiling was performed using the 10x Genomics Visium HD platform on four FFPE longitudinal tumor specimens from a single patient.
data_processing: Regions of interest were selected based on H&E quality and IHC data on immune cell infiltration from adjacent sections. RNA quality was confirmed by DV200 assessment prior to processing.

Two specimens were placed per Visium HD slide (6.5 × 6.5 mm capture area), and libraries were prepared according to the manufacturer’s protocol (Visium HD CytAssist Spatial GEX 6.5 mm workflow; 10x Genomics).
Libraries underwent Qubit fluorometric quantification and TapeStation fragment analysis and were sequenced on an Illumina NovaSeq (PE50), generating ~550M reads per sample.
FASTQ files were processed using Space Ranger (v4.0.1) with alignment to the GRCh38-2020-A reference and quantification using the Visium Human Transcriptome Probe Set v2.0.

CytAssist alignment images were registered to corresponding brightfield H&E images using the supplied JSON files with manual refinement using loupe Browser 9. Resulting feature matrices and spatial metadata were used for downstream analysis.
All four specimens were imported into Seurat, and one baseline sample with low transcript capture was excluded. Cells expressing <50 unique genes were removed.
Remaining cells were normalized using SCTransform with cell area (total 2-µm bins per cell) regressed as a technical covariate.
Cell clustering (resolution 0.8) and differential expression analysis enabled manual cell-type annotation.
Tumor cell identity was confirmed via inferCNV using immune cells as reference.
Putative T–myeloid doublets were subclustered (resolution 0.3) and reannotated. Final annotated cell maps were exported for spatial visualization in Loupe Browser.
